Aleven: Help-seeking behaviour in an intelligent tutor, including ineffective help-seeking strategies, can be modelled and evaluated against logs of student-tutor interaction.
Baker: Off-task behaviour of students in an intelligent tutoring system can be detected from system-usage logs, and it is associated with certain attitudes and motivations.
Graesser: Student questions during one-to-one tutoring can be classified, and the quality of the questions students ask was positively correlated with achievement once they had some tutoring experience.
Pennebaker: Word-category measures of written language show good internal consistency across samples and relate modestly to personality.
Crossley: Lexical indices computed from second-language learners' writing predict which proficiency level the learner belongs to.
Robbins: The paper develops probability inequalities and limit theorems for the behaviour of an entire sequence of random variables, the basis for statistical methods that hold over a whole sequence rather than at one sample size.
